summary: Modular monolith architecture: Angular frontend, Java (Spring Boot) backend, PostgreSQL database on AWS (EC2/ECS + RDS).

frontend.justification: Matches team language(s): typescript; well suited to fintech. Full framework with strong conventions and DI; favoured in enterprise teams.

backend.justification: Matches team language(s): java; well suited to fintech. Enterprise standard with deep ecosystem; heavier to run and slower to start with.

alternatives.choice: Serverless functions (AWS Lambda / Cloud Run functions)
alternatives.why_not: Scored lower on this scenario's specific priorities and constraints.
Weaker scaling story at the expected user volume.
Needs csharp, which the team does not list.

database.justification: Well suited to fintech; fits a balanced workload. The default relational choice: JSONB, full-text search, strong integrity, huge ecosystem.

tradeoffs: Vertical scaling first; very high write scale needs read replicas/partitioning.

hosting.justification: First-class support for the chosen framework(s). The most complete cloud: Mumbai/Hyderabad regions, every compliance programme; needs real ops skill.
tradeoffs: Real operational burden: patching, scaling, IAM, billing complexity.

supporting.justification: UPI, cards and subscriptions for India; PCI scope stays with the PSP.
Object storage with India regions; the default for uploads at any scale.
Framework-native auth (Django auth, Devise, Passport, etc.). No third-party dependency.

supporting.choice: Self-hosted open models (Ollama/vLLM on GPU VM)
supporting.justification: Keeps data in your own infrastructure; needs a GPU and real ops.
In-memory cache for hot reads, sessions and rate limits.
Managed queues, pay per request; zero broker operations.
Web frontend does not cover the required mobile platforms; Expo ships Android/iOS from one JavaScript/TypeScript codebase, reusing the backend API.
tradeoffs: Some native modules require ejecting from Expo.

supporting.justification: AWS-native CDN with India edge locations.
CI/CD next to the code; free tier covers small teams.
Self-hosted metrics and dashboards; full control, some ops.

assumptions: Compute scaled for >100k users (multiple instances / autoscaling)
Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote; real bills depend on traffic shape and discounts
